status.read_this_first: The designs/verdicts/plan below are the approved r1 design. Where they disagree with scripts/hud-capture/plan.mjs (r2) and docs/hud-capture/README.md, those win.
r2_changes: No animated ui-scale, font-size or height (Dota failed to load hud_reborn.xml on r1 C1): five static S packs (lower/top 70/70, 80/80, 90/90, 85/110, 95/120) with one Dota launch each; C1 is everything at 100 %.
Every @keyframes property is one Valve animates; one animation per panel; Valve chat.css is not replaced.
F-scale x5 and F-chat fallbacks are gone; F-bg stays.

session_2026_10_17.result: solved; preview on dev via HudCanvas (assets/dota-hud-capture)
findings: Blending is linear light (99.98 % of HUD samples within one level over grey, sRGB-byte model 81 %); grey #808080 reaches the screen as 129.

custom_ui.css rules never reach panels inside chat.xml: chat box cycle, chat fonts, chat box heights, the Expired override and production's chat font/height/background did nothing. Only #HudChat itself (place, width) moves.
Panorama's outer box-shadow also fills under the panel: the R blocks show the lower HUD over the ring colour, not over the world.
The world animates while paused (trees, light shafts, butterflies); Steam screenshots carry no cursor.
Colour-blind mode was on in C1 phase 1 (owner's setting); layers use phase 2, S and C2.
Moving while paused: hero portrait, level-up sparks, first ability pulse, #DayGlow (Valve's pulse kept running), TP counter.
The wash clone drew a flat #1620346c (its picture did not load); the wash law (linear multiply) holds within one level there and on the real #center_bg in C2.

designs.name: Capture-and-compose: Dota renders every HUD pixel; the browser only runs exact compositing math on layers matted from in-game frames
designs.summary:
Stop emulating Panorama. One capture pack (pak03_dir.vpk: Valve's custom_ui.css plus ~48 KB of our rules, and Valve's chat.css with two font-size lines removed) makes the paused game render itself in 66 states. A single 99 s Panorama @keyframes clock drives everything:
- a solid backdrop under the whole HUD: `DOTAHud #HUDElements { background-color }` cycling black K, white W, gray G (#808080) and transparent T;
- opacity, wash-color and ui-scale on exactly the panels our settings touch;
- a 6×6 px phase marker (Valve's unused `.GreenScreen` panel, top-left corner, plus `#splash_screen` top-right), so every screenshot names its own state.

The owner sets up a Keeper of the Light demo, pauses, types 3 chat lines and parks the cursor. A hosted PowerShell watcher presses F12 (Steam's 'Save an uncompressed copy' gives PNGs) until all 66 phases are collected. That is one session, about 3–4 minutes of capturing.

From the K and W frames every layer comes out exactly, per pixel and per channel, as P = b + a·D. The gray frame decides whether Panorama blends in sRGB-encoded or linear space. Each setting becomes exact algebra on captured layers:
- **Opacity:** `#center_bg` captured isolated (other center_block children at opacity 0), and everything above it captured at backdrop opacity 0, for all 4 shadow/flare states.
- **Tint:** a multiplicative wash law fitted on 4 known wash colours.
- **Hide toggles:** both states captured.
- **ui-scale:** captured at every 5% step in the same cycle, if Panorama animates ui-scale.
- **Chat:** each typed line captured at every font size 14–26 on its own font-size clock; position, background and Valve's hudchat fade mask computed.

Separate in-game T frames from the same paused moment are predicted by the same pure compose() the browser uses, aiming for ±1 per channel, so parity is proven before shipping:
- the plain game frame;
- the world with the HUD hidden;
- three preset frames (violet tint, 'compact', 'Прозрачный') that also move the chat.

A short fallback session covers the case where Panorama does not animate ui-scale or font-size. A working prototype of the phase table and CSS generator is in scratchpad/design/capture-compose/.

designs.name: Renderer parity: matte-calibrated Panorama emulator with a linear-light WebGL2 paint backend
designs.summary: Keep the XML/CSS→DOM emulator (xml.mjs, css.mjs, scene.mjs, hud.mjs) as the layout and cascade engine for Panorama, and make its pixels measurably equal to the game's. The owner's game gives us the ground truth as a layer. Capture packs (custom_ui.css rules, hero demo only) animate the background of #HUDElements, the bottom of the HUD's draw order, through black, white, #808080 and transparent plates, plus one world-only phase. All of this runs on one Panorama @keyframes timeline in a paused Keeper of the Light demo, and an unstyled Valve panel (#splash_screen) is turned into a phase marker so every PNG labels itself. Matting the black, white and gray plates gives the exact premultiplied colour and alpha of everything Panorama draws, with no world behind it and no lossy compression. A harness renders the emulator in the same state over the same plates. It reports error per region and per panel, the alignment offset of each panel, and how well each candidate model fits. With those mattes we identify each Panorama operation: blend space, wash-color, filters, gradients, shadow kernels, ui-scale, and text. Valve's own 95-valve.conf sets hintstyle=hintnone for text "rendered through Panorama/pango", so outlines are unhinted and can be reproduced in JS. The browser cannot paint to that standard: it composites in sRGB, its text depends on the visitor's OS, its blur kernels differ and it resamples images its own way. So painting moves to a small WebGL2 backend that takes the DOM layout as input. It composites in linear light on SRGB8_ALPHA8 targets, has its own Pango-like text with an exact-area rasterizer, uses fitted shaders, draws engine parts as matte sprites with real alpha, and downscales the final frame like a screenshot. The owner's part is three Dota launches, about 30–40 minutes in total. Expected result: about 2/255 or less mean error on the reference frame and on every measured setting. The honest ceiling: it matches one paused moment of one state, not the living game.

designs.name: Hybrid sprites: the game's own pixels placed on the emulator's layout (K/W/G matting, animated capture program, scale ladder, captured chat lines)
designs.summary:
The emulator in src/customize/panorama stays as the layout engine. It runs hidden and returns rectangles for the anchors (#center_bg/#center_block, #minimap_block, #topbar, #shop_launcher_block) and for the chat container and line boxes. It no longer draws anything you see. Every visible pixel comes from Dota itself, captured with a capture pak03 that replaces custom_ui.css for the session.

How the capture works:
- Valve's custom_ui.css text gets an appended "capture program": integer-% @keyframes that run on a fixed clock.
- The program cycles the background of #HUDElements through four states: transparent (world), black K, white W and grey G #bcbcbc.
- At the same time it shows one group of HUD "slices" at a time by animating opacity on the slice roots. Opacity does not change layout.
- A 20×20 colour beacon (#GameEndContainer moved to x 1900, y 300) encodes the slot number, so the decoder can sort screenshots on its own.
- The user pauses the demo (3D portrait, minimap and particles freeze; Panorama CSS animations keep running), parks the mouse and presses F12 after each change. Steam must save uncompressed PNG.

What the decoder does:
- Mattes each slice per pixel to premultiplied colour plus alpha in Panorama's measured blend space. The G background decides between linear and sRGB and finds additive pixels.
- Fits the wash-color model from calibration washes.
- Measures the anchor offsets at each scale-ladder point and the chat line boxes per font size.
- Exports lossless WebP sprites and a manifest.
- Validates itself: the slices composited over K/W must equal the in-game full HUD over K/W, and the composite over the captured world must equal in-game views (default, "clear", product tint, scales, chat).

Slices (layer granularity), in paint order: top (the whole #topbar), chat lines, left (#stackable_side_panels + #MenuButtons), map (#minimap_container), buffs, flareL, centerBg (the only backdrop visible with the default skin; it carries opacity and tint), coreA, flareR, coreB, shadows, shop.
- coreA: portrait, health/mana, abilities, inventory.
- coreB: TP/neutral container, unit name and badge, stats, XP ring.
- Settings that are booleans and sit inside other layers become captured variants:
  - bevel/nobevel for the shadows toggle, which also hides every #AbilityBevel, the one on the top bar's TP icon included;
  - lo/hi ends of Valve's infinite animations: DayGlow 0.1/0.3 and the Dota Plus frame glow 1px/4px.
- Continuous settings are applied in code: opacity and wash on centerBg.
- ui-scale uses a ladder of captured scales: lower 70/85/100, top 70/90/100/120. Every preset is exact; values in between are downsampled from the next larger capture.

Chat:
- Geometry comes from the emulator with the product chat rules, checked against real typed lines in game.
- Lines are game-rendered sprites per (language, line, font 14–26), captured from labels injected into an overridden chat.xml. The labels use Valve's own chat-line markup (dota_chatmessage_hud / _hudall tokens).
- Measured line heights, plus the background and the hudchat mask, are applied in the compositor.

Sessions: A (mandatory, 100%), B (lower 85 / top 120 + chat check + ui-scale probe), C (70/90), D (top 70 + real product tint/opacity/flares check + wash calibration), E (optional, English HUD texts). Draft generator, verbatim CSS, chat.xml block and tokens are written to scratchpad/design (capture-plan.mjs → out/).

verdicts.winner: Hybrid sprites: the game's own pixels placed on the emulator's layout (K/W/G matting, animated capture program, scale ladder, captured chat lines)
scores: Capture-and-compose: Dota renders every HUD pixel; the browser only runs exact compositing math on layers matted from in-game frames
Renderer parity: matte-calibrated Panorama emulator with a linear-light WebGL2 paint backend
Hybrid sprites: the game's own pixels placed on the emulator's layout (K/W/G matting, animated capture program, scale ladder, captured chat lines)
flaws: Capture-and-compose: the chat font-size cycle is dead on arrival. In assets/dota-hud/panorama/styles/chat.css:1490-1496, 'DOTAChat#HudChat .GameAllChat, .GameAlliesChat { font-size: 18px }' applies to the span that wraps the entire message (dota_russian.txt DOTA_ChatMessage_Hud: '…'). The design deletes only the .ChatTarget font-size lines (829, 1325), so the text stays at 18 px whatever font-size .ChatLine animates to. S1 then sees constant widths and must fall back to S2 static packs, with exact fonts only at about 6 sizes. Fix: also drop font-size at line 1495, which matches production hudRules, since it sets .GameAllChat/.GameAlliesChat explicitly.

Capture-and-compose: the README tells the owner to turn colour-blind mode off, but his reference 22.webp shows blue health/mana bars (516/516). The preview would then show green bars that differ from his own game. This must be an explicit owner decision (his game or Valve default), not a silent setting.

Capture-and-compose: 1.5 s phases with 0.25 s guards assume every animated panel (#lower_hud, #topbar, #center_bg, the GSIso targets, HudChat children) shares the marker's clock within about 0.25 s. Only the #HUDElements backdrop is checked against the marker. Any skew would silently mix states into the per-phase medians, or be mislabelled as 'particles'.

Capture-and-compose: there is no fallback for pixels clipped at 255 in the W frame (additive particles or glows). There a = φ(W) − φ(K) is underestimated, which turns additive into a screen-like blend over the world. Use K/G for those pixels, as Designs 2 and 3 do.

Capture-and-compose: the menu reuse ignores that hiding top-bar buttons (#TopBarCollection … #TopBarPlus) reflows a flow-children row. Toggle phases alone cannot cover 2^7 layouts without a layout model.

Capture-and-compose: one 66-phase pack (47.7 KB, about 840 stops) depends at once on unproven animatable properties: ui-scale, font-size, horizontal-align, y, width, height and visibility. Several will likely need S2, so the realistic owner time is S1 + S2 + S3, not 30 min.

Renderer parity: by construction it cannot be identical. It re-rasterises Panorama text with its own JS rasteriser and re-implements filters, shadows and mips, and its own gates (MAE <= 2, P99 <= 12) concede residuals the owner will see. world.webp from the world phase is saved at q90 lossy, so even the world under semi-transparent HUD is not exact.

Renderer parity: the scope '.HeroDemo #HUDElements' is unverified. The only Valve use is '.HeroDemo #ToggleCombatLogButton' (dota_hud_menu_buttons.css:72), which may be a class on DOTAHudMenuButtons, not an ancestor of #HUDElements. Also, opacity on #HUDElements itself is unproven, and the game already overrides visibility on that panel.

Hybrid sprites: matting stores a single alpha per pixel (median_c t). The Panorama fontconfig 50-base-rendering conf sets rgba=rgb with lcdfilter, so if HUD text is subpixel-rendered, colour fringes are lost. Over W, P + t·1 would then miss by the per-channel spread, and the FULLK/FULLW <= 2/255 gate would fail on glyph edges. Keep per-channel t (as Design 1 does).

Hybrid sprites: centerBg opacity is modelled only as group opacity, (P, α) → (o·P, o·α). center_bg draws background-color #1620346c and ability_bg_psd separately (hud_reborn.css:470-481). If Panorama applies opacity per draw, the result is quadratic in o, and there is no alternative model ready (Design 1 has one).

Hybrid sprites: ui-scale between ladder points (lower 70/85/100, top 70/90/100/120) is area-resampled from the next larger capture. Game text is re-rasterised natively, so values such as 80% or 95% are not identical, yet the sliders stay continuous.
Hybrid sprites: world.webp = A.V0 is used as is, with no cursor inpainting. The cursor parked at about (1820,600) gets baked into the preview world if the screenshot includes it.

Hybrid sprites: the beacon tolerance of +/-8 against code steps of 32 levels accepts frames up to about 25% into a 2 s linear fade. Correctness then rests on the background-sample checks; tighten the tolerance or add a guard colour.

Hybrid sprites: the top.bevel/top.nobevel variants and the claim of a bevel on the top bar's TP icon are wrong. Valve already sets '#TopBarTPIcon #AbilityBevel' and '.Reborn .TopBarIndicator #AbilityBevel' to visibility: collapse (dota_hud_ability_panel.css:2492, 2559). The variants are wasted slots, but harmless.

Hybrid sprites: chat.xml is a Valve layout shared by every DOTAChat instance, including menu and party chat. Overriding it to inject #GSCapLines risks a load failure; it is mitigated by collapse outside .HudChat and labels without handlers.

verdicts.winner: Capture-and-compose (one 66-phase capture session, the browser only composites matted game layers)
scores: Capture-and-compose (one 66-phase capture session, the browser only composites matted game layers)
Renderer parity (emulator calibrated against matted captures, painted by a WebGL2 linear-light backend)
Hybrid sprites (game pixels per slice, positioned by the emulator; ladder of static-scale sessions)
flaws: Design 1: Valve's 2004 CSS files never animate visibility, horizontal-align, ui-scale or font-size in @keyframes. ui-scale and font-size do appear in transition-property (13 and 2 uses), so they are probably animatable. visibility and horizontal-align probably are not. GSFlare mixes visibility with opacity, and GSChat mixes horizontal-align with y, width and opacity. If Panorama drops an unsupported property or the whole keyframes block, the flare-toggle and chat-geometry phases are lost. Put the unproven properties on separate probe elements.

Design 1: the single-clock assumption is unverified, and the 'both markers must agree' rule makes it fatal. #HUDElements stays collapsed until DOTAHud.IsInGame:not(.IsBeforeGameplay), and #lower_hud and #minimap_container until .ShowLowerHUD and .ShowMinimap. .GreenScreen is a DOTAHud child that our rule makes visible from creation. If Panorama starts animation clocks when a panel is first shown, the two markers and GSLower drift apart, and the watcher may reject every frame.

Design 1: the bevel buffer covers a delay of up to 7.5 s. Ability panels are created when the hero spawns, which in hero demo can be 10–30 s after the HUD panels are created behind the loading screen. With a larger delay, state/scale combinations such as A00 at ls95 never get captured, so the claim 'nothing is lost' is wrong.

Design 1: the top bar contains a DOTAAbilityPanel (TopBarTPIcon in dota_hud_top_bar_player.xml), which has its own #AbilityBevel. The TS120 top-bar layer comes from iso85 (phases 40–43, bevel block OFF) while the other scales come from bevel-ON phases, so the bevel state is inconsistent across top-bar scales.

Design 1: GSChatBox changes the height and background-color of #ChatLinesContainer, which has a Valve transition (chatTransitionDuration = 0.3 s). That is longer than the 0.25 s marker guard. The capture pack should set transition-duration to 0s there and on HudChat (position, 0.2 s).

Design 1: the chat lines run on their own font-size clock, so real.default shows chat at an arbitrary font size, not the default 18px. The system 'paused' line also appears in every validation frame and has to be masked.

Design 1: 2 F12 presses per second for 3–4 minutes leaves about 400–500 Steam screenshots (JPG plus PNG, roughly 2–3 GB) in the owner's library. Steam's hotkey rate and PNG write speed are unverified.

Design 1: the menu reuse ignores that hiding #TopBarCollection, #TopBarWatch and the other buttons reflows their row (these are RadioButtons in a flow). Compositing layers by region cannot reproduce the reflow.

Design 2: the '.HeroDemo #HUDElements' scoping is unverified. Valve uses .HeroDemo only as '.HeroDemo #ToggleCombatLogButton', inside #MenuButtons, so the class may sit on the menu-buttons panel. Then the P1, P2 and P3 plates all fail and an extra launch is needed.

Design 2: parity depends on re-implementing Panorama's painting and its Pango/FreeType text. Valve's conf.d holds the full infinality-style rule set (61-group-*, 80-selective-rendering-inf-*), not just hintnone. The MAE ≤ 2 target is not guaranteed, and 15–18 days is an underestimate.
Design 2: the 1% keyframe ramps (1.2 s) make the marker slide rather than jump, so the press 'about 1 s after the jump' can land inside the ramp. Uploads are 150–250 MB per zip, three times.
Design 2 and all others: tracks on panels inside #lower_hud (center_bg) can run on a different clock than the backdrop on #HUDElements. Ingestion checks only the backdrop and the marker.

Design 3: the integer-% grid gives 2 s linear fades, but the owner is told to press F12 once 'after each change', so a human press often lands mid-fade. Valve uses fractional stops (50.0001%, 99.9999%), so near-instant steps were available.

Design 3: beacon codes rgb(16+32(i%8), 16+32*floor(i/8)) with ±8 tolerance. During the 7→8 and 15→16 fades the interpolated colour passes within ±8 of the slot 6 and slot 14 codes, so frames can be misclassified when the backgrounds also match.

Design 3: the paint order contradicts itself. It states shadows at z-index 800 and the XP ring at z-index 1012, yet composites coreB (#xp z-index 1012, #death_panel_buyback z-index 1000, #multiunit z-index 1106) before the shadows. .AbilityInsetShadowLeft (margin-left 210) is next to #level_stats_frame (218) and the XP ring, so overlap is likely, and fixing it means re-slicing and capturing again.

Design 3: overriding chat.xml affects every DOTAChat, menu party chat included. The injected synthetic chat lines may not match the lines the game builds. The 60 s animation-delay counts from panel creation, which may happen during loading.
Design 3: values between ladder points (e.g. lower 75–80 or 90–95) are resampled, so they are not exact although the sliders are continuous. After a HUD patch, up to 4 sessions must be redone.

verdicts.winner: Capture-and-compose: Dota renders every HUD pixel; the browser only runs exact compositing math on layers matted from in-game frames
scores: Capture-and-compose (Dota renders every HUD pixel; browser runs compose() on K/W/G-matted layers)
Renderer parity (matte-calibrated emulator + linear-light WebGL2 paint backend + Pango-like text engine)
Hybrid sprites (game pixels on the emulator's layout; slices, scale ladder, captured chat labels)
flaws: Design 1's core bet has no precedent in Valve's files. It animates ui-scale, font-size, width/height, horizontal-align, margin and visibility inside @keyframes (session1-append.css GSLower/GSTop/GSChat/GSChatBox/GSChatFont). I counted the properties in all @keyframes across ~2000 Valve Panorama stylesheets (scratchpad 9fec1763…/dvu): ui-scale, font-size, width, height, horizontal-align and visibility each appear 0 times; only y appears (7). Transitions on ui-scale (13), width (173), height (243) and font-size (2) do exist, so it is plausible but unproven. The S2 fallback (up to 5 extra sessions) is a realistic branch, not a corner case.

Design 1: the capture pak03 is unscoped ('DOTAHud #HUDElements…') and the owner restores it by hand (step 12). If he forgets, his next real match flashes black, white and gray plates under the HUD. The watcher should back up pak03, refuse to run while dota2.exe is open, and restore it automatically.

Design 1's menu_reuse ignores reflow. Production hides top-bar buttons with visibility: collapse and 'the bar closes up' (scripts/menu-background.mjs MENU_HIDE comment). Hidden news cards also reflow the home page. Seven toggles give 128 layouts, and the design demotes the emulator to fallback-only, which leaves no layout engine to place per-button captures.

Design 1 bakes the owner's own Steam nickname and his typed lines into the public chat preview. The text is then frozen, and EN needs another session. Today's CHAT() uses neutral names (Администратор / Сын стиля / Кискадёр).
Design 1's byte-exact decode fallback names a 'JS PNG decoder', but the layers ship as lossless WebP. It needs either a JS WebP decoder or PNG copies.

Design 1's watcher presses F12 every 0.5 s for ≥160 s. That is 320+ uncompressed 1080p PNGs plus JPG copies (~1-1.5 GB on disk). Steam's screenshot hook may ignore an injected keybd_event, and the manual fallback of 2 presses/s for 3-4 minutes is tiring.
Design 1's compose() runs on the main thread at 10-20 ms per change. That is acceptable, but slider drags on weak devices would want a worker or WebGL.

Design 2: '.HeroDemo #HUDElements' scoping rests only on '.HeroDemo #ToggleCombatLogButton' (dota_hud_menu_buttons.css:72). If the class sits on #HUDElements itself rather than an ancestor, nothing matches and P1 is a wasted launch.

Design 2 has the highest owner burden: 3 launches, F12 pressed by hand at ~1 s and +2 s after each marker jump (~160 shots), and 150-250 MB per zip. It also delivers only a fitted approximation (target MAE ≤ 2, stated ceiling) after 15-18 dev-days, while the owner asked for an identical copy.
Design 2 cites scratch phases.json, but it does not exist in scratchpad/design. The only phases.json there is design 1's, in capture-compose/.

Design 3's hidden layout emulator still builds Valve's full scene. In Chrome, visibility:hidden elements still fetch their background images, so the page loads Valve textures and 0.58 MB of Radiance/Reaver on top of a ~4 MB sprite first view. It needs a layout-only mode with a texture-size manifest and no image fetch.
Design 3 needs 4-5 restarts, F12 pressed by hand after every on-screen change, and manual pak swaps (the helper is optional). Each restart is another chance for owner error.
Design 3 overrides Valve's chat.xml, which is shared with menu and party chat. A rejected override can break chat everywhere or crash at load, and the stated recovery is a Steam file check.
Design 3 leaves three render paths to maintain (hidden emulator, WebGL2/Canvas2D compositor, DOM fallback), plus sprite-key combinatorics (ladder × bevel × lo/hi × lang).

plan.rationale:
**Why capture-and-compose wins.** Judges 2 and 3 picked it (69.5 and 73); Judge 1 had it a close second (73.5 vs 76.5).

**Why the others lose:**
- **Renderer parity** re-rasterises Panorama/pango text and filters. By its own gates (MAE ≤ 2) it can never be identical, and the owner rejects "close".
- **Hybrid** gave the safest mechanics, but:
  - it slices into a single alpha per pixel, which loses LCD/subpixel fringes;
  - its paint order contradicts itself (coreB contains z-1000+ panels yet is composited under the z-800 shadows);
  - it overrides the shared chat.xml;
  - it resamples between ladder rungs.

  Its good ideas are grafted:
  - never depend on one animatable property;
  - capture DayGlow lo/hi;
  - layout-model reflow for the menu;
  - footprint/geometry pre-flight;
  - the separate-acceptance mindset.

**Every judge flaw is addressed:**
- **Chat font did not change.** Fixed by deleting the 1495 line too. The three deletions are verified to match exactly once.
- **Colour-blind is now an explicit dual capture.** In Valve's settings, ToggleButton dota_hud_colorblind sits in «Игра → Интерфейс», and .ColorBlindModeEnabled switches the health bar, top-bar health, stat colours and agility icon.
- **Clock skew.** Same-element marker and backdrop; guard scales; per-frame pixel classification; bevel on its own clock.
- **W clipping.** A local G at every scale (HON) provides the K/G fallback.
- **Unproven animatable properties.** Isolated in separate animations, with a live verdict and pre-built fallbacks in the same session.
- **Chat transitions.** Valve's chatTransitionDuration on height and background is neutralised: transition-duration 0s on HudChat, #ChatLinesContainer, #ChatLinesPanel and .Expired.
- **Pak safety.** The watcher refuses to run while dota2.exe is open, backs up and restores pak03 automatically (also on the next run if interrupted), and checks SHA-256.
- **Menu reflow.** Emulator layout plus per-button captures plus validation subsets.
- **Byte-exact decode.** 3-channel lossless WebP, createImageBitmap with colorSpaceConversion none, a self-test, and a lazy WASM libwebp fallback (not PNG).
- **compose runs off the main thread** (worker / OffscreenCanvas).
- **Scale steps.** Sliders snap to the captured 5 % steps, so no value is resampled.
- **Hybrid's top.bevel variants are dropped.** Valve collapses #TopBarTPIcon #AbilityBevel (dota_hud_ability_panel.css, the TopBarTPIcon list) and .Reborn .TopBarIndicator #AbilityBevel.

**Verified Valve facts the plan depends on:**
- DOTAHud > #HUDElements is 100%×100% with no background. It is collapsed until `DOTAHud.IsInGame:not(.IsBeforeGameplay)`; that specificity, not C++, explains why our earlier `visibility: collapse` lost.
- HUDElements child order: topbar, …, HudChat, …, minimap_container (z 2), splash_screen, lower_hud (z 2), NetGraph, …, stackable_side_panels, …, MenuButtons.
- DOTAPaused has z-index −1. .GreenScreen is a DOTAHud child after #HUDElements; with z-index −1 it can serve as the fallback backdrop.
- #center_block has no flow-children, so collapsing flares or insets cannot reflow anything.
- #center_bg is #1620346c plus ability_bg_psd. Only center_bg is visible without .Reborn.CustomHUDSkin.
- #ChatMainPanel uses flow-children down and vertical-align bottom, so a taller chat box grows upward from a fixed bottom.
- Valve keyframes use fractional stops (99.9999 %, 50.0001 %, 33.32/33.33 %), so our 0.01-s steps are idiomatic.
- :nth-child is supported (ability_details_v2.css).
- Infinite HUD loops visible at level 1 (OpacityPulse on #LevelUpGlow, borderglow5 on the Dota Plus #RecommendedUpgradeOverlay .BorderEdge, DayNightPulse) are frozen at their 0 % keyframe. DayGlow alone is captured lo/hi, because opacity is affine, so its pulse can be crossfaded exactly.

**Geometry is pre-checked against the existing emulator:**
- #lower_hud box is y ≥ 574 at 100 % (726 at 70 %);
- default chat box is 497..659 with about 201 px of controls below it;
- C1's chat (left 40, y −437) puts the box at about 280..442;
- the clone is at 1180..1669 × 200..345;
- cursor A is at about (1780, 270) and B at about (1780, 540): clear of every region and of the ring band.

captures.in_game:
Шаги 5–11 инструкции.

plan.user_instructions_ru:
Съёмка интерфейса Dota для конструктора — одна сессия, примерно 30–40 минут. Из них около 10 минут ты просто ждёшь.

Как это работает: на время съёмки скрипт подменяет твой pak03 тестовым пакетом. Под интерфейсом мигает чёрный и белый фон, панели меняют размер, а скрипт сам делает скриншоты. В конце он возвращает твой pak03 на место.

ПОДГОТОВКА (один раз, ~5 минут)
1. Steam → Settings → In Game → Screenshots (в русском Steam: Настройки → В игре → Снимки экрана):
   • «Take a screenshot» — оставь F12;
   • выключи «When a screenshot is taken, display a notification» и «When a screenshot is taken, play a sound»;
   • включи «Save an external copy of my screenshots» и выбери папку C:\GSShots (создай её заранее);
   • включи пункт «Save an uncompressed copy» — несжатая копия в PNG. Он появится ниже. Это обязательно: из JPG ничего не выйдет;
   • если включён счётчик FPS Steam («In-game FPS counter») — выключи его.
2. Настройки Dota не меняй: 1920×1080, обычный HUD без скина. «Режим цветовой слепоты» оставь как есть — мы снимем оба варианта.
3. В строках чата будут твой ник Steam и тег гильдии, и они попадут в превью на сайте. Если не хочешь — поменяй ник на время съёмки.
4. Закрой Dota. Открой PowerShell (Пуск → набери PowerShell → Enter), вставь команду и нажми Enter:
   irm https://dev.gridstudio.me/hud-capture.ps1 | iex
   Скрипт сделает всё сам:
   • найдёт Dota;
   • переименует твой pak03_dir.vpk в pak03_dir.vpk.gs-backup;
   • положит тестовый пакет №1;
   • спросит папку скриншотов (ответ: C:\GSShots).
   Окно PowerShell не закрывай до самого конца.

СЪЁМКА 1 (~10 минут)
5. Запусти Dota → Герои → Keeper of the Light → «ОПРОБОВАТЬ». Ничего не покупай и способности не изучай: жёлтые «+» над способностями должны остаться.
   В демо всё будет выглядеть странно — так и задумано:
   • фон под интерфейсом мигает: чёрный, белый, игра — каждые полторы секунды;
   • нижняя и верхняя панели меняют размер и иногда пропадают;
   • левой панели демо не видно.
   Если мигание неприятно, на экран можно не смотреть.
6. Поставь паузу клавишей F9. Надпись «Игра приостановлена» скрыта пакетом, поэтому проверь по часам вверху экрана: они должны остановиться. Если не встало — нажми F9 ещё раз (или набери в консоли: dota_pause).
7. Уже на паузе напиши в чат три строки. Больше в чат ничего не пиши.
   • Enter → го рошан → Enter
   • Shift+Enter → gg wp → Enter
   • Enter → нужна мана → Enter
8. Поставь курсор в точку А:
   • у правого края экрана, отступив от края на 3–4 см;
   • по высоте — на четверть экрана сверху;
   • над землёй, не над юнитами и не над интерфейсом.
   После этого мышь и камеру больше не трогай.
9. Нажми F12 один раз. В окне PowerShell пойдёт счётчик снимков, и дальше скрипт сам жмёт F12 примерно каждые 0,75 секунды.
   Не сворачивай Dota через Alt+Tab, иначе скрипт перестанет жать.
   Если через 10 секунд счётчик не растёт или ты слышишь длинный гудок — жми F12 сам примерно раз в секунду, пока не услышишь двойной сигнал.
10. Примерно через 2,5 минуты будет ДВОЙНОЙ сигнал. Тогда:
   • открой настройки (шестерёнка вверху слева), в поиске настроек набери «слепоты» и нажми «Режим цветовой слепоты»: был включён — выключи, был выключен — включи. Закрой настройки;
   • поставь курсор в точку Б: так же у правого края, но на середине высоты экрана. Мышь больше не трогай;
   • нажми F12 один раз — скрипт продолжит сам.
11. Ещё примерно через 3–4 минуты будет ТРОЙНОЙ сигнал: съёмка 1 готова. Выйди из матча (меню → «Покинуть игру» или «Отключиться») и закрой Dota полностью.
   Дальше скрипт сам скажет, что делать. Иногда какая-то часть пакета не срабатывает, и он просит запасную съёмку — тогда делай, как он пишет. Каждая запасная — это повтор шагов 5–9 и около минуты ожидания, Dota между ними перезапускается.

СЪЁМКА 2 — проверка (~5 минут)
12. Когда скрипт напишет «Запусти Dota», запусти её → Keeper of the Light → «ОПРОБОВАТЬ». Интерфейс теперь другой, и так надо: подложка нижней панели голубоватая и полупрозрачная, панели другого размера, чат посередине на тёмном фоне.
13. Нажми F9, напиши те же три строки чата (как в шаге 7), поставь курсор в точку А и нажми F12 один раз. Примерно через минуту будет тройной сигнал — закрой Dota.
14. Скрипт вернёт твой pak03_dir.vpk на место и соберёт архив gs-hud-capture.zip (около 0,6–0,8 ГБ) на рабочем столе.
   • Проверь, что в Steam\steamapps\common\dota 2 beta\game\dota_russian снова лежит твой pak03_dir.vpk.
   • Внутри архива файлы уже названы автоматически (C1_0001.png…, C2_0001.png…, session.json) — ничего не переименовывай.
15. «Режим цветовой слепоты» потом верни, как тебе удобно.
16. Загрузи gs-hud-capture.zip на 0807.st как файл и пришли ссылку. Не через Telegram: он пережимает картинки, и вся точность пропадёт.

ЕСЛИ ЧТО-ТО ПОШЛО НЕ ТАК
• Длинный низкий гудок — загляни в окно PowerShell: там написано, что случилось и что делать.
• Окно скрипта закрылось раньше времени или выключился компьютер — запусти ту же команду ещё раз. Первым делом она вернёт твой pak03.
• Скрипт совсем не запускается — пришли текст ошибки. Если хочешь, можно сделать всё вручную:
   1) переименуй свой pak03_dir.vpk в pak03_dir.vpk.bak;
   2) возьми pak03_dir.vpk из папки C1 архива dev.gridstudio.me/hud-capture/hud-capture.zip и положи в game\dota_russian;
   3) пройди шаги 5–11, нажимая F12 вручную примерно раз в секунду;
   4) повтори то же с папкой C2;
   5) верни свой pak03 и упакуй все PNG из C:\GSShots, сделанные за эту сессию, в один zip.
• JPG-скриншоты в библиотеке Steam после съёмки можно удалить.
pipeline:
Classify every frame from its own pixels. No clock is trusted. Per frame:
- **Global backdrop:** exact K, W or T at the free points (1000,250), (1100,520) and (1700,420).
- **Lower ring:** found on column x = 1500 between y 450 and 800. Its colour gives the block and the guard/core part. Its row, clustered into 7 levels, gives the lower scale. No ring means the lower HUD is hidden.
- **Lower local backdrop:** K/W/G/T at (1500,800) and (1560,900).
- **Child-panel state:** center_bg zone, flare zones and inset strips, using probes learned per scale from the ring-labelled majority. Frames whose children disagree with the ring block are dropped; the guards absorb offsets up to 3 s.
- **Bevel:** on/off per ability and item slot, by 2-cluster on the slot zone.
- **Top bar:** scale, clustered into 11 extents, and DayGlow lo/hi from the glow brightness.
- **Chat:** box state (L, M250, M100 or hidden), each line's font (ink-width clusters, 13 levels) and line bands.
- **Wash clone:** one of 9 colour clusters at (1424,272).
- **Colour-blind state:** health-bar hue.
- **Cursor box:** A or B.

Blend space φ. On HON local K/W/G at every lower scale, test φ ∈ {sRGB-encoded, linear}. The G frame must equal b + a·φ(128/255) within ±1 on at least 99.9 % of HUD pixels under exactly one φ. This also proves the HUD is composited affinely over our backdrop. Stop and report if neither φ fits.

Fits. Each is a choice between named hypotheses, with residuals reported:
- **Wash law** on the clone: multiply or lerp, sRGB or linear, wash applied before or after opacity.
- **Opacity model:** group-linear, or per-draw quadratic with the known #1620346c colour layer. Fitted on the clone at 0.35 and 0.55 and on the real #center_bg (RCLR 0.35, RCMP 0.70).
- **World compositing law:** UI over world, premultiplied over in φ or alternatives. Fitted on RDEF/RCLR/RCMP global-T frames against the assembled world.
- **Chat mask sampling:** bilinear stretch of Valve's 3×239 hudchat_mask_psd under the box's scaleY(−1). Fitted on heights 100, 162, 250 and 400.

Every compose term is division-free:
- shadows on: b = b_A1 + t·M⊙(b_H1 − b_A1), a = a_A1 + t·(a_H1 − a_A1);
- the quadratic model and lerp washes are also expressible with no divisions;
- low-alpha pixels therefore never amplify noise.

Validation report, with gates. Outputs: an HTML report in the scratchpad and a private A/B page on dev.
- **(a) Plates:** in global-K/W frames, and wherever a region is hidden, every pixel equals the plate exactly. This proves the backdrop sits over the world and under the HUD; whatever is drawn above it gets listed.
- **(b) G consistency.**
- **(c) Real views:** RDEF, RCLR and RCMP over the world against compose(): at least 99.5 % of HUD pixels within ±1.
- **(d) C2:** the HUD matte against compose(C2 setting), and C2's T frames against compose over C2's world. Zones that depend on the pause moment (clock, TP cooldown digits, timer rings, portrait pose) are masked.
- **(e) Static = animated:** C1's lower 85 and top 110 layers against C2's, in zones the setting does not touch. Also C2's collapse against C1's opacity 0.
- **(f) Chat:** geometry, mask and background at 400 px / 22 px / 50 %, centred.

Per region the report gives MAE, P99, % within ±1, heatmaps and the top error panels. The owner gets an A/B flicker page against his own PNGs.

scripts/hud-capture/plan.mjs: port of scratchpad/design/final/plan.mjs and gen.mjs.
- Contents: slot tables, marker colours, the stepped-keyframe generator (0.01-s steps), and builders for C1, C2, F-bg, F-scale×5 and F-chat.
- Self-checks: value at every segment midpoint, unique stops, period sums, ASCII.
- C2's production block comes from hudRules(C2_SETTING) in scripts/hud-style.mjs.
- scripts/hud-capture/chat-css.mjs: the three-declaration chat.css edit, each regex asserted to match exactly once.

scripts/make-hud-capture.mjs, modelled on scripts/make-interface-test.mjs.
- Fetch Valve's custom_ui.css and chat.css from spirit-bear-productions with the same fetchText and s2r→_c fix-up.
- Build 9 pak03_dir.vpk files with buildVPK and panoramaResource (version 2, md5).
- Write manifest.json (name, sha256, size), plan.json for the solver and a Russian ПРОЧТИ.txt.

tests/hud-capture-plan.test.cjs.
- Plan invariants:
  - every 3 consecutive global slots hold a K and a W;
  - every non-hidden block has guards;
  - marker colours differ by at least 20 levels per channel.
- Every selector exists in assets/dota-hud/panorama layouts.
- The freeze list equals the mechanically derived set of Valve rules with an infinite animation-iteration-count that match in the default emulator scene; anything missing fails the test.
- Geometry pre-flight with the emulator rects:
  - C1 chat box (about 280..442 at 162 px) clear of the #lower_hud box (from 574) and of the top bar (up to about 156 at 120 %);
  - the clone rectangle, cursor A/B and the ring band are free.

Dev hosting: deploy-dev.sh publishes /hud-capture.ps1 and /hud-capture/** as static files. An nginx `location ^~ /hud-capture/` plus an exact `/hud-capture.ps1` location. Check both /hud-capture and /hud-capture/ with curl (the prefix-slash 301 lesson). Never run `nginx -t -c` with a custom conf.

scripts/hud-capture-solve.mjs, plus modules scripts/hud-capture/{ingest,classify,stability,matte,fit,layers,world,validate,export}.mjs. They implement the pipeline and write assets/dota-hud/capture/** and the report.

src/customize/panorama/HudCanvas.jsx, used by HudScene.jsx.
- Draw the world once; recompose only the HUD rectangles.
- Lazy-load layers per scale, showing the nearest loaded level until the exact one arrives.
- Byte-exact decode: createImageBitmap with colorSpaceConversion 'none' and premultiplyAlpha 'none', 3-channel images, a startup self-test on a known pattern, and a lazy WASM libwebp lossless decoder if the bytes differ.
- 1:1 zoom.
- DayGlow pulse: 2.94 s linear 0.1→0.3→0.1, crossfading lo/hi in φ.

per_setting.default_view:
Exact by construction. Every Panorama pixel is the game's own per-channel matte, checked by G frames, at lower 100 / top 100. It is composited in the measured blend space over the world captured in the same paused moment (world assembled from hidden-region frames; cursor removed by the A/B swap). That includes the 3D portrait, minimap, top-bar hero, innate icon, Dota Plus frame and the level-1 skill-point state, all drawn by Dota. Proven by C1's RDEF frames over the world and by the plates.

Valve's endless loops (Dota Plus recommended-ability glow, level-up glows) are frozen at their 0 % keyframe: a real still frame of the game. #DayGlow pulses exactly through the lo/hi crossfade. Colour-blind mode is captured both ways: the site defaults to Valve's green, and a toggle shows the owner's blue. Target: at least 99.5 % of HUD pixels within ±1 per channel, at most 0.5 % flagged (particles, portrait idle).
per_setting.opacity: Exact for 0–100 at 1 % steps. Division-free compose from H/A layers at the selected scale. The model, group-linear or per-draw quadratic with Valve's #1620346c colour layer, is chosen on the clone (0.35/0.55) and on the real #center_bg (RCLR 0.35, RCMP 0.70), then validated by C2 (0.55 + wash, static production rule). Without a custom HUD skin only #center_bg is visible (#HUDSkin* are collapsed unless .Reborn.CustomHUDSkin), so the slider changes only center_bg, exactly as in the game.
per_setting.tint: The wash law is fitted per pixel on the clone (#arcana_container styled exactly like #center_bg). It covers 6 washes (#0000008c, #ff0000ff, #00ff0080, #8a5cff73, #2fa8ff4d, identity) and 2 opacity combinations. Candidates: multiply or lerp, sRGB or linear, wash before or after opacity. Validated on the real #center_bg in C2 (#2fa8ff4d at 0.55). Any colour and strength comes out within ±1 if a law fits; otherwise interpolation over the clone samples gives about ±2–3, reported in the validation.
per_setting.hide_toggles: Flares and shadows (inset strips plus every #AbilityBevel) are exact at every captured scale. H1/A1 (on) and H0/A0 (off) are captured per lower block; flare zones and inset strips are spatially disjoint; bevels are captured on/off per slot on their own 48-s clock. Top-bar bevels are already collapsed by Valve. C2 proves production's visibility:collapse renders identically to opacity 0; #center_block has no flow-children, so nothing reflows. Statue (DOTAHeroStatue.Visible inside #QueryUnit) and team items (.CommonItemsTitle inside the closed shop) are not on screen in the in-match default view. The preview shows no change, as the game does; C2 includes both hides to prove it, and the UI copy says so.
per_setting.ui_scale: Exact at every 5 % step: lower 70–100, top 70–120. The sliders snap to those values, so nothing is resampled. Each level is a separate game rendering, with re-laid-out text and the 3D portrait and minimap re-rendered. C2 proves animated = static at lower 85 and top 110. If ui-scale does not animate (live verdict), the five F-scale packs give lower {70, 80, 85, 90, 95, 100} and top {70, 80, 90, 100, 110, 120} exactly, and the sliders snap to that set.

plan.menu_plan:
The same machinery serves the main menu, after the HUD ships:
- the generator (plan.mjs);
- the watcher;
- the solver (classify, matte, fit, world);
- compose and HudCanvas.

**Capture variant of our pak02 (scripts/menu-background.mjs pack).**
- Inside our DOTADashboardBackgroundManager override, a solid capture panel under the dashboard UI cycles K, W and T. A local G gives the φ check.
- Our #GridStudioMovie runs at opacity 0 during K/W and is visible in T.
- A box-shadow marker on the same panel carries the slot code.
- The menu's looping glows are frozen at their 0 % keyframe with the same mechanical freeze-list test.
- Private panels (friends, party, avatar, nickname, guild) go to opacity 0 through their own tracks. They are never shipped; neutral rendered stand-ins replace them.

**Pages.** The owner opens the home page, then «Герои», with the cursor parked over empty space. That is one Dota launch of about 3 minutes per page. The watcher uses the same F12 automation.

**Hide toggles and reflow.** The top-bar buttons (#TopBarCollection, #TopBarWatch, #TopBarLearn, #TopBarMods, #ShardsButton, #TopBarArmory, #TopBarPlus) and the news cards are hidden with visibility:collapse, so their rows reflow.
- Positions come from the existing emulator's layout of dashboard.xml and the page XML (a flow model). It is checked against captures with no hiding and with two static subsets: the product's default hide set and an alternate one. Those are two extra short launches.
- Pixels come from per-button and per-card mattes cut from the all-visible capture.
- If the emulator's flow positions are off, the per-element widths and margins measured from the captures replace them.

**Backgrounds.** Our own background video or image is the exact base layer, because it is our file. The loading screen works the same way: our MoviePanel is the base, and Valve's tips and progress overlay is matted.

**What is not exact.** Static chrome is exact. Live content (news, events, store) is a snapshot of the capture day.

**Upkeep.** check-dota-menu.mjs already watches dashboard.xml; its hashes flag a recapture.

**Effort.** About 4–5 dev-days plus one 20-minute owner session.
open_risks:
**ui-scale, font-size or height may not animate in Panorama.** No Valve @keyframes uses them, though ui-scale and font-size do appear in Valve transitions, including 'transition-property: ui-scale'. Each is isolated in its own animation and the watcher reports it live.
- Fallbacks in the same sitting: F-scale (5 launches, about 15 min) and F-chat (1 launch).
- Degraded result: lower {70, 80, 85, 90, 95, 100}, top {70, 80, 90, 100, 110, 120}, even chat fonts.
- With F-scale, the colour-blind variant exists only at 100 %.

**An animated value might render differently from a static one** (composition-layer caches, e.g. the always-cache-composition-layer panels). C2 detects this at 85/110. If it fails, a follow-up session with static ladder packs is needed; that cannot be decided live.
**#HUDElements' background might not paint.** The F-bg fallback uses .GreenScreen at z-index −1. If neither paints, the run stops and we ask for a screenshot.

**Child panels on another animation clock.** If center_bg, the flares or the insets run on a clock more than 3 s away from #lower_hud's, the guards stop absorbing it. The classifier detects this and drops frames, and the watcher extends the run by another lower cycle. Simulation of ±3 s and a ±30 s minimap offset gives 100 % completion.

**Geometry is estimated with the emulator.** The real #lower_hud top and chat controls height may differ (chat box about 280..442 against the lower box from 574 at 100 %). If the chat box intersects the lower box, those chat frames are matted against the wrong backdrop: they are detected and dropped, and a chat-only re-run may be needed. The pre-flight test and the first-minute verdict reduce this risk.
**Steam may ignore the synthetic F12** (SendInput). The owner then presses F12 by hand about once a second for about 6 minutes; the watcher detects this within 10 s.

**The paused world may not be static** (foliage wind, water, ambient butterflies). Medians and variance masks handle it. Varying world pixels come from one real frame. Unit overhead bars or any Panorama world overlays drawn above our backdrop show up in the plates and are treated as world.

**Particles that animate during pause** (LevelUpBurstFX, NeutralBurstFX) and any portrait idle cannot be matted per frame. Base = temporal minimum plus a one-frame overlay; opaque engine panels use the K frame. These pixels are flagged and excluded from the ±1 gate.
**The wash law might not be a standard form.** The clone samples allow an interpolated LUT (±2–3), shown in the report. The opacity model is resolved between the two hypotheses by data.

**Valve's looping glows stay static in the preview** (Dota Plus recommended border, level-up glow), shown at their 0 % keyframe: an exact still but not animated. Animating them would need an extra pulse capture. DayGlow is the only loop animated exactly.

**The preview is one specific state:** Keeper of the Light demo at level 1, the RU client, the owner's Dota Plus, his nickname and guild tag in the chat lines, clock and TP cooldown at the pause moment. Other heroes, the open shop or statue, English texts and other resolutions are not covered. An English run (-language english) would be a later optional C1 repeat.
**Dota updates make the captures stale.** check-dota-menu flags it; a re-run of C1 + C2 takes about 25 minutes.

**Owner errors:** JPG-only setting, mouse moved, Alt+Tab, accidental F12 during setup, chat flood protection. The watcher checks format, detects backdrop and cursor anomalies and stretches phases. Worst case: redo C1.
**Upload and disk:** about 0.6–0.8 GB per zip (0807.st allows 10 GB), plus about 200 MB of Steam library JPGs.

**Preview weight:** about 8–10 MB of lossless layers in total, lazy-loaded. The first view is about 4 MB, mostly the 3 MB lossless world. A browser decode mismatch is caught by the self-test and the WASM fallback.

**The capture pak is not scoped to the demo.** The only Valve .HeroDemo use is on a menu button, not an ancestor of #HUDElements. Safety therefore relies on the watcher restoring pak03 in try/finally and on its next start. The owner is told to re-run the command if the window was closed.
